access_details: Visitors have two options to access Valley Creek. From State Highway 21, approximately 8.5 miles west of Stanley, take the M-M Sportsman Access turn and drive .8 mile. The other option is to access Forest Service Road 682 from State Hwy 21 and proceed to the foot access turnoff. Both options provide walking access to Valley Creek. Offsite camping is available at nearby Sawtooth National Recreational Area campgrounds.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: Camping is limited to no more than 10 days within any 30 day period. Pets must be on a leash at all times. Fires only in approved fire pits. Please pack out what you pack in.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: Much of the surrounding area is private property; please obey all signs and markers. Please, no pets allowed. Campfires not allowed Access is limited to foot traffic only. Please pack out what you pack in. Day use only.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: Camping is limited to no more than 10 days within any 30 day period. Pets must be on a leash at all times. Please pack out what you pack in
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This 2-acre Sawtooth National Recreational Area access is located 2.5 miles west of Stanley along State Highway 21. It provides a graveled parking area within easy walking distance to Valley Creek. Daylight use only.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This 2-acre site provides public access across Thompson Creek Mine private lands to the Salmon River. Four to five campsites are available. Limited turnarounds restrict access to RVs over 30 feet long.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: Much of the surrounding area is private property; please obey all signs and markers. Pets must be on a leash at all times. Campfires not allowed. Access is limited to foot traffic only. Day use only. Please pack out what you pack in.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This Idaho Department of Lands undeveloped access provides boating access to the Salmon River. Parking space is limited at this natural boat ramp and is available at turnouts immediately south along US Highway 93.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This 4.5 acre access provides camping, fishing and boating access to the Salmon River. Picnic tables and grills are available at some of the sites. A turnaround area and spacious, shaded camp sites provide access for most RVs. Winter fishing for whitefish is good on this reach of the Salmon River.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public
IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: Camping is limited to no more than 10 days within any 30 day period. Much of the surrounding area is private property; please obey all signs and markers. Pets must be on a leash at all times. Please pack out what you pack in.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: Camping is limited to no more than 10 days within any 30 day period. Please pack out what you pack in..
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This access is a partnership between the City of Challis and IFG which provides convenient access for persons with disabilities and accessible family fishing within walking distance of downtown Challis. Follow 2nd Street South to the end of the road and take the paved path to the pond. You will find sheltered picnic tables and benches arranged around the pond. The pond is stocked with rainbow trout as well as excess hatchery steelhead in the spring.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This access provides roadside parking along State Highway 21 within easy walking distance to Valley Creek. For more information on Sawtooth National Recreation Area access, campgrounds and permitted uses, contact the Stanley Ranger Station, located 2.5 miles south of the intersection of State Highways 21 and 75.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This 9-acre Sawtooth National Recreational Area access is located alongside State Highway 75 and offers easy parking for six or eight vehicles just walking distance from the Salmon River. Limited camping space and turnarounds are available. Please respect the private property that borders this access.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: A short hike from the parking area along a well–maintained trail takes you to Jimmy Smith Lake. From there, an unimproved trail along the north side of the lake takes you to BLM and Forest Service lands. It is a popular year-round trout fishing and fall hunting destination. Camping is limited to two dispersed sites along the 2- mile access road which forks off the East Fork Road. Turnaround space and RV camping is limited at the trailhead parking area.from the lake provides foot and horse access only to adjacent federal lands.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: Camping is limited to no more than 10 days within any 30 day period. Pets must be on a leash at all times. Please pack out what you pack in. Groups of 15 people or larger must obtain a permit at the IDFG Regional Office.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: Camping is limited to no more than 10 days within any 30 day period. Pets must be on a leash at all times. Please pack out what you pack in. Groups of 15 people or larger must obtain a permit at the IDFG Regional Office. Gravel boat ramp available.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This 198-acre access provides abundant fishing, hunting, and wildlife viewing opportunities. A disabled fishing platform is located at the southwest access. Check the “Special Rules Waters” section of the Idaho Fishing Seasons and Rules for restrictions on the Pahsimeroi River. Short-range weapons only are allowed during all hunting seasons. Please stay within the posted boundaries out of respect for our ranching neighbors.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

water_name: Salmon River and accesses BLM lands
access_details: This is an IFG public easement through private land that provides a natural boat ramp to the Salmon River and accesses BLM lands. Wildlife viewing opportunities are numerous here. Please respect adjacent private properties and stay within the posted boundaries.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This public fishing pond is provided for the enjoyment of our young anglers. Please observe the following. Fishing Rules: State fishing rules and regulations apply. Please consult the current Idaho Fishing Seasons and Rules Book (available at the hatchery or any local license vendor) for additional information. Age Restrictions: This pond is for children 17 years of age and under. Parking Information: Parking is restricted to the visitor parking lots. Fishing Hours: 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Some fishing equipment is available. Please inquire at the office.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This 8-acre access has a pond which is occasionally stocked with rainbow trout during the summer fishing season, especially for the Memorial Day and July 4th holidays. Water for the pond is from a secondary water right, so the pond is periodically drawn down by irrigators during the summer. A 150-foot walk from the parking area is required to access the pond. Limited camping space is available at the Squaw Creek Access located just east of the US Highway 93 and Squaw Creek Road junction. Daylight Use Only.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This IFG foot access-only easement across private land offers fishing access to Valley Creek. The easement extends approximately 400 feet east of the bridge on the south bank of Valley Creek. Please stay within the posted easement boundaries. Daylight use only.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: IFG regularly stocks this reservoir with rainbow trout. A Forest Service developed campground and boat ramp are located on the east side of the reservoir.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This 12-acre access offers 12-15 primitive camping sites and a restroom. It is a popular destination for camping, steelhead fishing, big game and chukar hunting.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This BLM, 1-acre unimproved site provides a natural boat ramp with additional parking across US Highway 93. It is popular with spring steelhead and summer salmon anglers.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This 1-acre IFG/Elk Bend Fire Department access provides a developed boat ramp access to the Salmon River and parking for about 8 vehicles. Approximately 1-mile south on US Highway 93, turn east up Warm Springs Creek and drive a short distance to a parking area. A 1-hour hike up a maintained trail takes you to Goldbug Hot Springs, one of the nicer public land hot springs in the Salmon Region. Daylight Use Only.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: The Ellis North (Idaho Department of Lands) and Ellis South (Bureau of Land Management) accesses follow the Salmon River’s southeast bank near the mouth of the Pahsimeroi River. Both accesses are popular fishing destinations for steelhead and salmon anglers. Boating access to the river is available two miles upstream at the Cottonwood BLM Campground.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: The Ellis North (Idaho Department of Lands) and Ellis South (Bureau of Land Management) accesses follow the Salmon River’s southeast bank near the mouth of the Pahsimeroi River. Both accesses are popular fishing destinations for steelhead and salmon anglers. Boating access to the river is available two miles upstream at the Cottonwood BLM Campground.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: IFG holds a 30-foot wide by 2.25 mile long access easement along the west bank of the Salmon River. To access the Easement, go into the Deer Gulch Access, turn left, then follow the road bearing right up and over the foothills to the north entrance. Access from the south is by foot over the Sweeny Bridge. Dogs on leash only.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This 8 acre access offers eight or nine primitive campsites and a natural boat ramp bordering the Salmon River. It is popular yearround.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This 14-acre access is owned and managed by the City of Salmon. Plenty of parking space is available in addition to picnic tables, two boat ramps, benches, and a restroom with running water March 1 - November 30. The park is open from 6 a.m. until 10 p.m. daily.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This unimproved, 3.5-acre access is located behind the Sungate Apartments off Margaret Street next to Saveway Market in Salmon. It provides foot access to the Lemhi River just walking distance from town for trout fishing or wildlife viewing. Park your vehicle at the end of Margaret Street and walk to the river bank behind the dike. Please respect the private property surrounding this access. Check the “Special Rules Waters” section of the Idaho Fishing Seasons and Rules for restrictions on the Lemhi River.Daylight Use Only.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public
IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This 100-foot wide, daylight use only IDFG walking easement through private land follows the southwest side of the Lemhi River from Highway 28 to BLM’s McFarland Recreation Site. Please stay within the posted boundaries and respect the neighboring ranchers’ private property. Camping and amenities are available at BLM’s McFarland Recreation Site.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This 4.5-acre access was donated to IDFG by Winn and Betty Turner. It is a popular access for summer boaters and spring/fall steelhead anglers. Plenty of parking space is available for boat trailers, but camp sites are limited to three or four RVs. In 2008, IFG and their non-profit partners built a bighorn sheep viewing station. Sheep frequently cross this section of US Highway 93 so please drive carefully.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public
IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: A disabled angler’s fishing ramp at this BLM Recreation Site was constructed in part with IFG Steelhead and Salmon permit funds. This is a fee area with designated parking, camping, and restroom facilities. A detachment led by William Clark of the famed Lewis & Clark Expedition camped at the Tower Rock site in August 1805 while completing a reconnaissance of the Salmon River.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This 8-acre access offers one of the best natural boat ramps on the Salmon River. Six shaded camp sites are scattered along the river bank as well as ample parking, making this a very popular yearround destination.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: Located 26 miles southeast of Salmon along State Highway 28, this 5.6 acre access provides a nice camping area for six or eight units. It borders the Lemhi River and has trees for shady campsites, making it quite popular during the summer camping and fall hunting seasons. Camping and turnaround space is adequate for most RVs. Check the “Special Rules Waters” section of the Idaho Fishing Seasons and Rules for restrictions on the Lemhi River.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

water_name: Hayden Creek Road 3 miles south of the State Highway 28 junction
access_details: This access is located along the Hayden Creek Road 3 miles south of the State Highway 28 junction. The ponds are managed for year-round trout fishing and regularly stocked with rainbow trout. This is a very popular family spot with a restroom, pavilion, picnic tables, grills, and a restroom. The spring which feeds the ponds is warm enough to prevent ice build-up even during the coldest winter temperatures.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: Located in the Salmon city limits just off US Highway 93, this 1.75- acre site co-managed by IFG and the City of Salmon is a popular fishing pond for young anglers. The pond is regularly stocked with catchable rainbow trout and excess hatchery steelhead or salmon during spring and summer. The access contains a fishing dock, a pavilion with picnic tables, and a number of benches around the well-maintained lawn. A restroom and trash containers are provided. Daylight Use Only.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This less than 1-acre Idaho Department of Lands roadside access is located 21 miles east of Salmon off State Highway 28 and offers Lemhi river access. The site is unimproved and offers no amenities with limited camping and turnaround space for RVs.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This unimproved, .75-acre access offers parking for two or three vehicles along US Highway 93, with foot access to the Salmon River. There is a steep unimproved trail down to the river’s edge.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This unimproved Idaho Department of Lands and BLM site offers parking and foot access to the Salmon River with space to tent camp below the road or park an RV above.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This 198-acre access provides abundant fishing, hunting, and wildlife viewing opportunities. A disabled fishing platform is located at the southwest access. Check the “Special Rules Waters” section of the Idaho Fishing Seasons and Rules for restrictions on the Pahsimeroi River. Short-range weapons only are allowed during all hunting seasons. Please stay within the posted boundaries out of respect for our ranching neighbors.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This IFG/private land lease agreement provides access to the Salmon River. It is located behind the North Fork Store and Campground, 22 miles north of Salmon off US Highway 93. Private campsites and picnic sites are available adjacent to this access. Daylight Use Only.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

water_name: Salmon River about 5-miles downstream from the City of Salmon
access_details: This IDFG 12-acre site provides boating and fishing access to the Salmon River about 5-miles downstream from the City of Salmon. It is a popular access for summer boaters and spring/fall steelhead anglers.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

water_name: Salmon River and hunting access to public lands
access_details: This 55-acre access provides fishing access to the Salmon River and hunting access to public lands. There are spacious camping sites, a covered pavilion, disabled angler’s ramp, and three separate restroom facilities. This is a very popular camping spot for RVs and tents alike.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This Idaho Department of Lands unimproved site offers a natural boat ramp with limited parking and camping space. Please respect adjacent private property when parking along the McKim Creek Road.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

access_details: This 2.5-acre access offers primitive camping below US Highway 93. There is a beach area at low water along the Salmon River. A small boat could be launched here with difficulty. The road is unimproved and steep. Camp trailers and RVs are not recommended.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public

water_name: confluence of the Lemhi and Salmon Rivers off US Highway 93
access_details: This 5-acre access is located at the confluence of the Lemhi and Salmon Rivers off US Highway 93. It provides vehicle and foot access to the Salmon River and is a popular steelhead fishing destination. A restroom, plenty of parking, RV camping, and turnaround space are available.
official_source_name: IDFG Fishing and Boating Access Sites Public
